cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:1-2). He's just warned that the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil, and that some who crave it have wandered away from the faith (1 Timothy 6:10). Then he turns to Timothy: "But you, O man of God," and friend, when somebody starts with "But you," you sit up STRAIGHT.

cards.question: After warning about the love of money, Paul tells Timothy, the man of God, to ___ from these things.

cards.text: Flee means FLEE, not back away slowly while you're still staring at it. Then Paul hands Timothy a list: righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance and gentleness.

cards.question: Righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance and gentleness. What does Paul tell Timothy to do with that list?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Fight the good fight of the faith." A FIGHT, friend, and here I am with nothing but a mustache, putting up my dukes anyway.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to take hold of the ___ life he was called to.

cards.text: Paul reminds Timothy when that call came. It was the day he made the good confession.

cards.question: Timothy made his good confession in private, with no one else around.

cards.text: Then Paul gets SERIOUS: he charges Timothy in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus. That's not a "hey, when you get a chance" text, friend; that's the boss walking over to your desk in person.

cards.question: Paul says Christ Jesus made the good confession too. In His testimony before whom?

cards.text: That's Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor (Matthew 27:2). And look at that: "the good confession," the same words Paul just used for Timothy.

cards.question: Paul charges Timothy to keep this commandment without stain or reproach. Until when?
Paul gives Timothy a date for when Jesus Christ will appear.

cards.text: No date, and I don't guess either: I just keep the ovens warm (Matthew 24:36). It comes in His own time, brought about by the blessed and only Sovereign One, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
And I think Paul's just warming up. He says God alone is immortal, and He dwells in unapproachable light.

cards.question: Paul says that over the years, a few people have seen God.
After describing God like that, how does Paul wrap up this part of his letter?

cards.text: After his Amen, Paul circles back to money, with instructions for those who are rich in the present age. Friend, I was bought for a quarter, but I'm listening anyway.

cards.question: Paul tells the rich not to be conceited, and not to put their hope in wealth, but in ___.
Paul describes wealth as something uncertain.

cards.text: And Paul says God richly provides all things for us to enjoy. He wrote ENJOY, friend, so if anybody asks why I'm grinning at a tray of chocolate chips, I've got backup.
Then Paul gives the rich their to-do list, starting with: do good. And then he flips the word "rich" right around on them.

cards.question: Paul tells the rich to be rich in something besides money. What is it?
Paul also tells the rich to be generous and ready to ___.

cards.text: Giving money away sounds like watching it walk right out the door. Paul says nope: they're actually treasuring something up for themselves.

cards.question: When the rich are generous, what does Paul say they treasure up for themselves?

answers.text: A firm foundation for the future
A good name in the city

cards.text: All so that they may take hold of that which is truly life. There's "take hold" again, just like when Paul told Timothy to take hold of eternal life.
Then Paul puts an "O" in front of his name: "O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you." When somebody puts an "O" in front of your name, friend, you stop scrolling.

cards.question: As he finishes his letter, what does Paul tell Timothy to avoid?
Paul says some people who professed this so-called knowledge swerved away from the faith.
Paul ends the whole letter with a short blessing. What does he say be with them all?

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Save them for later" doesn't hold up as a real option. Nobody would believe Paul tells Timothy to put off righteousness, godliness, faith and love. It reads as silly, not as a believable wrong answer, and it doesn't match the tone of the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card calls Pilate "the Roman governor" and cites Matthew 27:2. That verse only says "Pilate the governor." It doesn't say Roman, so the reference doesn't support the fact as stated. Either drop "Roman" or cite a verse that supports it.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Several cards say Paul speaks to the rich directly: card 2 ("Paul tells the rich not to be conceited"), card 5 ("Paul gives the rich their to-do list"), card 6 ("Paul tells the rich to be rich") and card 7 ("Paul also tells the rich"). In the text, Paul tells Timothy to instruct them: "Instruct those who are rich…" (6:17) and "Instruct them to do good…" (6:18). The cards should say Paul tells Timothy to instruct the rich.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Long trips and late nights" is modern lifestyle advice, while the right answer, "Empty chatter and opposing arguments," sounds like Scripture. That makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question says "this so-called knowledge," but no card ever tells the baker about "so-called knowledge." Card 12's answer only says "opposing arguments." So "this" points back to something the baker never saw, and that part of verse 20 is never told.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question asks what Paul says should "be with them all," but no one has said who "them" is. The text actually says "Grace be with you all," with "you" meaning the readers. "Them" has no clear referent and changes who is being addressed. The wording "What does he say be with them all?" is also awkward.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
